i0000.variation: The base methodology, BUT isolation is measured at cluster depth, not pair depth: a candidate's isolation term is the mean distance to its k nearest other unvisited cities, with k a small tunable integer (the base's pair-depth rule is the k=2 point). A remote cluster of three or more cities is invisible at pair depth for the same reason a pair is invisible at single-nearest depth — its members are mutually close — yet the whole cluster still forces an end-of-tour detour. Sweep k over a small range (2, 3, 4) jointly with w in the base's iteration loop; keep the (distance-to-current − w·isolation) selection rule and everything else unchanged.

i0001.variation: The base methodology, BUT the isolation weight is a schedule over tour progress, not a constant: w(t) interpolates from w_early to w_late as the fraction of unvisited cities falls. Early, positive weight collects strays while the tour still passes near them; late, isolation pricing has little left to save, and w_late may cross zero into negative territory — recovering this line's look-ahead bias toward cities whose onward hop is cheap, exactly when short hops are all that remain. The two endpoints (w_early, w_late) are the tunables, swept on a coarse signed grid per the base loop; linear interpolation in remaining-fraction unless a two-phase step scores better.

i0002.variation: The base methodology, BUT extend the base's leftover bands into a tier ladder derived from the scorer's item distribution: classify a prospective leftover by the expected NUMBER of future items it can still absorb — zero (dead), exactly one (a residual below twice the minimum item size, which can take at most one more item and should be held for a matching close rather than nibbled), or two-plus (live). Hard score offsets separate rungs and tightest-first orders within each, except the exactly-one rung prefers residuals near the middle of the item range, where a future match is most probable. All band edges are calibrated against the canonical instance generator per the base, never hard-coded.

i0003.variation: The base methodology, BUT the avoid band's edges are live state, not calibrated constants: a leftover is truly dead exactly when it is smaller than the smallest item that can still arrive, so recompute the dead threshold from the instance itself — the minimum of the remaining item sizes when the interface exposes them, else the running minimum observed so far. As small items are consumed the dead band widens and marginal bins effectively close, so the same placement can be live early and dead late. Keep the base's hard tier offsets and cheap bin-closing rule; only the tier boundaries move with the instance.

i0004.variation: The base methodology, BUT go from measuring pair-level loneliness to acting on it: score each candidate by a depth-two rollout of the base rule — the cost of moving to c plus the best immediate follow-up from c under the same (distance − w·pair-depth-isolation) objective. A detected remote pair is thereby swept in one committed two-city excursion instead of hoping two independent greedy choices line up, and a candidate whose best continuation is expensive is demoted even when it looks cheap one step out. w stays the single weight, shared by both rollout steps and tuned per the base loop; rollout depth is fixed at two to keep per-step cost quadratic.

i0005.variation: The base methodology, BUT extend hard tier dominance to the decision the tiers currently ignore — opening a new bin: treat a fresh bin as an explicit candidate with its own tier, ranked above any placement whose leftover would land in the nearly-dead band. When every feasible existing bin would strand nearly-dead space, deliberately open a new bin rather than lock the loss in; near-perfect closes and live best-fit placements still outrank opening, so the escape fires only against the dead tier. Band edges are calibrated against the canonical instance generator per the base, and whether the scorer's interface permits refusing feasible bins is verified in step 1 before building on it.

i0006.variation: The base methodology, BUT the avoid band's dominance is annealed over the instance: a nearly-dead leftover is only costly while enough items remain for the stranded capacity to be missed, so scale the tier offsets by the fraction of items still to come — full hard dominance early, decaying smoothly to plain best-fit over the final placements, where refusing a snug fit merely scatters the last items across extra bins. Band edges and the closing threshold are calibrated against the canonical instance generator per the base; the one new tunable is the onset fraction below which the offsets start shrinking, left to the iteration loop.

i0007.variation: The base methodology, BUT replace per-bin leftover shaping with a portfolio rule over the whole set of open bins: keep the multiset of remaining capacities extreme rather than middling. Tight placements (prospective leftover under the 0.1 minimum item size) are scored by best-fit as usual; placements leaving a live leftover are scored in REVERSE - roomier survivors beat middling ones (score -0.3 + 0.2*leftover) - and any placement into the bin currently holding the maximum remaining capacity pays a flat 0.2 penalty, reserving the portfolio's largest slot for items nothing else can take. The one deliberate change: the score is population-aware and non-monotone in leftover (inverted on the live branch), instead of any refinement of per-bin leftover classes.

binpack.variation: The base methodology, BUT replace the parent's proportional dead-space score-shaping with a hard three-tier band around the scorer's 0.1 minimum item size, with the avoid region extended ABOVE that minimum: (1) if a bin's prospective leftover is under ~0.07, treat the bin as closed and take the tightest such fit - tiny stranded gaps are a cheap price for closing a bin; (2) hard-avoid leftovers in the nearly-dead band [0.072, 0.13), which either strand close to the maximum unusable space (below 0.1) or leave a sliver only near-minimum items in a razor-thin window can use; (3) otherwise plain best-fit. Tiers are separated by large score offsets so the band actually flips placements instead of collapsing to best-fit, while within-tier order stays tightest-first so forced choices remain sensible.

tsp.variation: The base methodology with the parent's strandedness pricing, BUT isolation is measured at pair depth: a candidate's isolation term is the mean of its distances to its TWO nearest other unvisited cities, not the single nearest. A remote pair of cities scores near-zero isolation under the single-nearest measure - each has the other close by - yet the pair as a whole is stranded and still forces nearest-neighbor's end-of-tour detour; averaging in the second-nearest distance exposes pair-level loneliness so such pairs are also collected in passing. Everything else follows the parent: pick the city minimizing (distance-to-current - w*isolation), w is the only tuning knob, tuned per the base loop - one change at a time, keep the best canonical score, stop after two consecutive non-improvements.
